articles.summary: Maharashtra UCC row: Owaisi alleges 'Hindu Civil Code' being imposed to target Muslims Mid-Day
articles.content: All India MajliseIttehadul Muslimeen AIMIM President Asaduddin Owaisi on Tuesday criticised the Maharashtra governments proposed Uniform Civil Code UCC alleging that the move was aimed at targeting Muslims and imposing a Hindu Civil Code on nonHindu communities news agency ANI reportedAddressing a press conference Owaisi said the Mahayuti government had invited public opinion on the implementation of the UCC and prepared a questionnaire for the consultation He claimed that the questions indicated that the Devendra Fadnavisled government had already decided to implement the codeWATCH Mumbai AIMIM President Asaduddin Owaisi says The subject of the press conference today is that the Maharashtra Government has invited opinions from the public to implement UCC The state government has also prepared a questionnaire for it This questionnaire prepared by the Maharashtra government makes it clear that the Devendra Fadnavis govt will implement the UCC The questionnaire consists of leading questions on polygamy and extrajudicial divorce But there is not one question on Hindu Undivided Family This makes it evident that much like the initiatives introduced by BJP governments in Gujarat Uttarakhand Assam and Madhya Pradesh under the guise of a Uniform Civil Code this is not a true UCC but rather a Hindu Civil Code that is being imposed upon nonHindu communities Additionally if you examine the questionnaire you will find that the majority of the questions are framed in a yes or no format I believe this is precisely why RC Chavan a retired judge of the Bombay High Court chose to resign He had stated that there is no one from the minority community They are talking about implementation in the state of Maharashtra at this juncture but they are not defining what this uniform actually ismdash ANI ANI November 10 2026The subject of the press conference today is that the Maharashtra Government has invited opinions from the public to implement UCC The state government has also prepared a questionnaire for it This questionnaire prepared by the Maharashtra government makes it clear that the Devendra Fadnavis govt will implement the UCC he saidOwaisi Gujarat Uttarakhand Assam and Madhya Pradesh claiming that these were not uniform civil codes but attempts to impose a Hindu Civil Code on nonHindu communitiesOwaisi calls proposed UCC a Hindu Civil Code imposed on nonHindusThis makes it evident that much like the initiatives introduced by BJP governments in Gujarat Uttarakhand Assam and Madhya Pradesh under the guise of a Uniform Civil Code this to elicit yesorno responsesAdditionally if you examine the questionnaire you will find that the majority of the questions are framed in a yes or no format he addedOwaisi also linked the resignation of articles.title: Aaryavir Sehwag's 160 blitz blows UAE away, sends India into U19 Asia Cup semis - India Today
articles.summary: Aaryavir Sehwag's 160 blitz blows UAE away, sends India into U19 Asia Cup semis India Today
articles.content: Brief Scores: India-U19 (3097 in 50 ovs) beat UAE-U19 (2399 in 50 ovs) by 70 runs to qualify for the semifinal of the U19 Asia Cup. Aaryavir Sehwag (160), VK Vineeth (67); Ishan Sood (337); HighlightsThe Sehwag surname has long been associated with attacking batting in Indian cricket. Virender Sehwag made a career out of taking on bowlers from the outset, often setting the tone with his fearless approach. His son Aaryavir, however, showed that he has a way of his own. Against UAE on Tuesday, the young opener took his time at the start, built his innings patiently and then shifted gears to produce a commanding 160.His knock powered India U19 to a 70-run win in the U19 Asia Cup and secured their place in the semi-finals against Afghanistan. After suffering a defeat to Pakistan in their previous outing, India needed a response. Aaryavir gave them the perfect platform.AARYAVIR ANCHORS INDIAUAE won the toss and elected to field, hoping to make the most of the early assistance on offer. The surface had a tinge of moisture and an even covering of grass, with the new ball expected to help the pacers. India needed their top order to show patience, and Aaryavir did just that.The opener began cautiously as UAE's seamers found movement and kept the scoring in check. India lost captain Lakshya Rajesh Raichandani for 17, but Aaryavir held his ground. He also survived a couple of chances, with UAE unable to hold on to opportunities, but made sure to make the most of his reprieves.VK Vineeth joined him at the crease and the pair gradually took control. They added 193 runs for the second wicket, turning India's steady start into a substantial platform. Vineeth played the supporting role with a fluent 65, while Aaryavir continued to accumulate runs without taking unnecessary risks.As he settled in, Aaryavir began to find the boundaries more regularly. He used his feet against the spinners, picked his shots carefully and punished loose deliveries. The change in tempo was clear after he reached his hundred. Having spent the first part of his innings getting his eye in, he began to attack with greater freedom.His innings eventually ended at 160 off 168 deliveries, with 17 fours and seven sixes. It wasn't an all-out assault from the first ball. Aaryavir built his innings in stages, showing an approach quite different from the one that made his father famous.India lost Aaryavir in the 45th over, caught at mid-wicket off Naseem Khan, but the damage had been done. The lower order added useful runs in the closing overs, with Mohit Ulva finishing the innings with a six. India reached 309 for 7, registering the highest total of the tournament at that stage.UAE FIGHT BACKChasing 310 was always going to be a demanding task, particularly against an Indian attack with a sizeable total to defend. UAE, however, did not fold without a fight.India made early inroads and kept the asking rate under pressure, but Ahmed Khudadad and Noorullah Ayobi gave their side a chance to make a contest of it. Khudadad led the resistance with 74 off 74 balls, striking six fours and three sixes. Ayobi added 39 from 25 deliveries, injecting urgency into the chase.The pair's stand briefly raised hopes of an unlikely turnaround. Yayin Rai also chipped in with 29, but UAE needed a much bigger contribution from their middle order to sustain the challenge.India's bowlers kept chipping away at the wickets, ensuring the required rate continued to climb. The late partnership had threatened to make the finish uncomfortable, but India found the breakthrough when it mattered.SOOD SEALS THE WINIshan Sood proved to be India's standout bowler, finishing with figures of 4 for 37. He broke the resistance by dismissing Ayobi and Khudadad in successive deliveries, swinging the momentum firmly back India's way.Sood struck twice in the final over as well. He bowled Hadayatullah Khan to bring UAE's innings to an end at 239, sealing a 70-run victory for India.After the disappointment against Pakistan, India had delivered the response they needed. Aaryavir's 160 gave them the platform, Vineeth's contribution helped build the total and Sood led the bowling effort when UAE threatened to fight back.The comparisons with Virender Sehwag will follow Aaryavir as he makes his way in the game. But this innings offered a glimpse of his own approach. He may carry the same surname, but he showed he doesn't need to bat exactly like his father. He took his time, read the conditions and then went after the bowling. The result was an innings that put India into the last four.- Ends

articles.title: Owaisi Questions Maharashtra Govt’s UCC Questionnaire - Deccan Chronicle
articles.summary: Owaisi Questions Maharashtra Govt’s UCC Questionnaire Deccan Chronicle
articles.content: Hyderabad: AIMIM President Asaduddin Owaisi has said the Maharashtra government has invited opinions from the public to implement UCC and it has also prepared a questionnaire for it. The questionnaire, prepared by the Maharashtra government, makes it clear that the Devendra Fadnavis government will implement the UCC. The questionnaire consists of leading questions on polygamy and extra-judicial divorce. But there is not one question on Hindu Undivided Family. This makes it evident that, much like the initiatives introduced by BJP governments in Gujarat, Uttarakhand, Assam, and Madhya Pradesh under the guise of a 'Uniform Civil Code,' this is not a true UCC, but rather a 'Hindu Civil Code' that is being imposed upon non-Hindu communities. “Additionally, if you examine the questionnaire, you will find that the majority of the questions are framed in a 'yes or no' format. I believe this is precisely why R.C. Chavan, a retired judge of the Bombay High Court, chose to resign,” he explained. He had stated that there is no one from the minority community. They are talking about implementation in Maharashtra at this juncture, but they are not defining what this 'uniform' actually is."

articles.title: Baby Sehwag hits daddy hundred as India return to form in U19 Asia Cup - India Today
articles.summary: Baby Sehwag hits daddy hundred as India return to form in U19 Asia Cup India Today
articles.content: Aaryavir Sehwag, son of legendary India opener Virender Sehwag, scored a sensational daddy hundred (150-plus runs) in India's U19 Asia Cup match against UAE on Tuesday, November 10. Batting on a tricky pitch that kept low, seamed and spun at different stages of the game, Aaryavir showed immense maturity to navigate the innings and put India in total control.India, who were playing their first match in the U19 Asia Cup 2026 since their debacle against Pakistan, found a steady hand in Sehwag, who soaked up the pressure in the first hour of play before slowly putting India in command.Batting on a wicket that seamed profusely in the first hour, Aaryavir patiently notched up his half-century in 69 balls.U19 Asia Cup Live: IND vs UAE Photo: BCCIHis innings gradually gathered pace as the wicket settled down a little, allowing him to start playing his shots against the fuller deliveries. Sehwag switched gears when the spinners came on. He used his feet to charge down the wicket and lift them over the ropes through the covers. When the ball was pushed fuller, he got down and slog-swept it through the leg side.He brought up his century with a single through the square, reaching the milestone in 131 balls. After getting to three figures, Sehwag really ripped into the UAE bowling attack.Batting against left-arm wrist-spinner Uddish Suri, Sehwag slog-swept him for 21 runs in the 38th over, rapidly accelerating India's scoring after their slow start.At the other end, VK Vineeth also batted patiently, putting India in command with a half-century off 60 balls.Sehwag reached 150 in the 42nd over with a lofted on-drive over long-on, getting to the milestone in 160 balls.Sehwag's innings was important for India's confidence after they were battered by Pakistan in their previous match of the tournament. In the process, he also became the highest individual scorer in this edition's tournament. Screengrab: SonyLivAaryavir's innings came to an end in the 45th over of the match, when he tried to hit medium pacer Naseem Khan over mid wicket. He was caught inside the circle when India were at 255.His innings of 160 included 17 fours and 7 sixesA VERY DIFFERENT SEHWAGAaryavir's batting style looked very different from that of his father, Virender. While his dad was famous for his 'stand and deliver' style of batting, relying heavily on hand-eye coordination, Aaryavir is more of a classical opener. He relies on soaking up pressure before taking the attack to the opposition, using his feet and the depth of the crease to good effect.Aaryavir is particularly good against spinners and has a variety of strokes with which he disrupts the length of the slower bowlers.Whatever his mode of destruction, the baby Sehwag showed that he could be as effective as daddy Sehwag, producing a well-crafted hundred in the U19 Asia Cup.- Ends

articles.title: India's Pollution Crisis Hits Sports: Chennai Open Tennis Final Postponed Amid Heavy Smog - Business Today
articles.summary: India's Pollution Crisis Hits Sports: Chennai Open Tennis Final Postponed Amid Heavy Smog Business Today
articles.content: India's post-Diwali pollution surge has disrupted more than just daily life. The Chennai Open women's singles final between defending champion Janice Tien and Magda Linette was postponed after rain delays were followed by heavy smoke from Diwali fireworks engulfing the stadium. Tien shared an Instagram story showing the smog and an AQI reading of 1,556, raising fresh concerns over the conditions at the venue. The incident adds to a growing list of sporting events affected by India's pollution crisis, including cricket fixtures that have faced postponements or venue changes amid poor air quality. As the Chennai Open approaches its final edition, the disruption has cast a shadow over the tournament's farewell.

articles.title: What is the Gokul Cooperative Milk Federation election issue in Maharashtra? | Explained - The Hindu
articles.summary: What is the Gokul Cooperative Milk Federation election issue in Maharashtra? | Explained The Hindu
articles.content: Election to one of Maharashtra’s largest milk federations has turned into a political slugfest. Kolhapur Zilla Sahakari Dudh Utpadak Sangh Ltd, known as Gokul, is one of Maharashtra’s largest and most influential dairy co-operatives. After the election to the directors’ positions was held recently, the Congress-led panel won by a wafer-thin majority of 13-12 in a body of 25 directors. Soon thereafter, the BJP-led State government passed an order to appoint five nominated directors. Four of them will have voting rights. articles.summary: Rain keeps India waiting as New Zealand get another lifeline India Today
articles.content: India's wait for a series-clinching victory will continue after persistent rain washed out the third ODI against New Zealand at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Tuesday. Even after the toss was completed and the match was reduced to 40 overs per side, the weather refused to clear, leaving the umpires with no option but to abandon the contest without a ball being bowled.Shubman Gill won the toss for the third consecutive time and opted to bowl, with India retaining the same playing XI. New Zealand made one change, bringing in Matt Fisher for Blair Tickner. There was a brief window of optimism as the groundstaff prepared the playing area, but another spell of rain put paid to any hopes of a start.New Zealand vs India, 3rd ODI: UPDATESThe washout means India remain 2-0 ahead in the five-match series, having won both opening matches through the DLS method. The first ODI in Auckland was reduced to 32 overs per side, with India chasing a revised target of 143 to win by five wickets. The second match in Wellington was also shortened, with India securing a four-run victory on DLS after being left at 113 for seven in their chase of 135.The teams now move to Mount Maunganui for the final two ODIs, scheduled for November 13 and 15 at Bay Oval. With the third match abandoned, India will need one more win to seal the series, while New Zealand must win both remaining games to level it.WILL RAIN SPOIL REMAINING NZ VS IND ODIs?After rain affected the first two matches and wiped out the third, the weather will remain a talking point as the series moves to Mount Maunganui. The forecast for Friday's fourth ODI is more encouraging, with mostly sunny conditions and only a minimal chance of rain. Sunday's outlook for the series finale is less reassuring, with a 55 per cent chance of precipitation and cloudy conditions expected. The forecast could change closer to the matches, but another interruption cannot be ruled out.The Hamilton washout was particularly frustrating for India, who had hoped to wrap up the series with two matches to spare. Instead, the final leg now carries greater significance for both sides, with the weather potentially having another say in the outcome.BIG SQUAD CHANGES COMING UPThe final two ODIs will bring a change in leadership for India. Shubman Gill and KL Rahul will leave the ODI group to join the preparations for the Test series, with Shreyas Iyer taking over as captain and Ishan Kishan named vice-captain. Tilak Varma, Kumar Kushagra, Auqib Nabi and Yash Thakur are among the players included in the squad for the last two matches. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli remain available.New Zealand will also field a different group, with several players leaving for Test preparations. Tom Latham, Daryl Mitchell, Henry Nicholls, Glenn Phillips and Nathan Smith are among those moving across to the red-ball squad. Finn Allen, Lockie Ferguson and Tim Seifert are part of the group coming in for the final two ODIs, alongside Kristian Clarke, Matt Fisher, Mitch Hay and Nick Kelly.The changes add another layer to the series equation. New Zealand have won their last 11 bilateral ODI series at home, with their previous series defeat coming against India in 2019. That record is now under threat. The hosts must win both remaining matches to level the series and avoid defeat, while India need just one victory to secure a series win and a good boost for their 2027 World Cup prep.- Ends

articles.title: India A series ends in draws, Bumrah and Jadeja left short of match practice - India Today
articles.summary: India A series ends in draws, Bumrah and Jadeja left short of match practice India Today
articles.content: India's preparations for the upcoming two-Test series against New Zealand received mixed returns as the three-match unofficial Test series between India A and New Zealand A ended without a result. While several batters made strong statements ahead of the senior team's assignment, rain disrupted the final two games and denied some of India's key players the opportunity to build match fitness.The third and final unofficial Test in Lincoln ended in a draw on Tuesday after rain washed out the entire fourth day. The third day's play had also been abandoned without a ball being bowled, leaving the teams with little opportunity to make a contest of the match. All three games in the series ended in draws.India A had declared their first innings at 464 for five, with Yashasvi Jaiswal leading the charge with a century. Sai Sudharsan, Tilak Varma, Dhruv Jurel and Washington Sundar also made significant contributions, while New Zealand A were 36 for two when the match was interrupted.The series was intended to provide valuable red-ball preparation ahead of the first Test, which begins on November 19 in Wellington. Several players in the A squad are in contention for places in the senior team, while Jasprit Bumrah and Ravindra Jadeja were included in the final game to get some much-needed time in the middle after breaks from competitive cricket.JAISWAL, PADIKKAL LEAD THE POSITIVESJaiswal was among India's biggest gains from the series. The opener scored 102 in the final game, taking his tally to 279 runs in five innings at an average of 69.75. It was his second century of the series, underlining his strong red-ball form ahead of the New Zealand Tests.Devdutt Padikkal also made a compelling case in the race for India's No. 3 position. His 199 in the opening unofficial Test was the standout batting performance of the series, while Sudharsan kept the pressure on with two half-centuries, including an 88 in the final match and a fighting 91 in the first.Jurel added another strong performance with 71 in the third game, following a century earlier in the series. With Rishabh Pant still recovering from a side strain, Jurel's form could prove important as India assess their wicketkeeping options. Tilak Varma, who is not part of the senior Test squad, also impressed with an unbeaten 81.Akash Deep's return to action was another positive. The pacer is working his way back after a lengthy injury lay-off, while Prasidh Krishna also got an opportunity to bowl in the final match after recovering from a hamstring injury. He picked up both New Zealand A wickets to fall.BUMRAH, JADEJA MISS OUT ON GAME TIMEThe biggest disappointment from India's perspective was the lack of match practice for Bumrah and Jadeja. Both were expected to use the final unofficial Test to prepare for the two-match series, but the weather severely restricted their involvement.Bumrah, who last played in the Asian Games final against Pakistan on October 3, managed only six overs in Lincoln, conceding 11 runs without taking a wicket. He had been rested for the white-ball leg of the New Zealand tour to keep him fresh for the Tests and would have ideally wanted a longer bowling workload before the series.Jadeja, meanwhile, faced 71 deliveries for his 25, spending around an hour and 20 minutes at the crease. However, he did not get a chance to bowl as India A managed only 14 overs in the match. The all-rounder had joined the squad after featuring in two Ranji Trophy matches for Saurashtra.The duo will now travel to Wellington with the rest of the Indian contingent, where the team is scheduled to have six training sessions before the opening Test, weather permitting. Bumrah, Jadeja, Jaiswal, Padikkal, Sudharsan, Washington and Akash Deep are among the players expected to join the senior squad.- Ends
